conditions: Ranks are only an approximation of a two-step sequential swap; apply the steps below instead of the ranks.

Step 1 (OKC/HOU swap, HOU top-4 protected): if HOU's pick is in slots 1-4, HOU keeps its own pick and OKC keeps its own and MIA's (MIA's pick is owed to OKC unprotected). If HOU's pick is 5-30, OKC takes the two most favorable of {OKC, MIA, HOU} and HOU gets the least favorable of the three.

Step 2 (HOU/BKN swap, unprotected): after step 1, HOU may exchange any first-rounder it holds (its step-1 pick, plus POR's pick if it conveys past top-14 protection, plus DET's pick if it conveys past top-16 protection) for BKN's pick; HOU therefore swaps its least favorable held pick for BKN's if BKN's is more favorable, and BKN receives the displaced pick.
The rank allocation above reproduces steps 1-2 only when HOU's pick is outside the top 4, BKN's pick is not better than OKC's two picks, and POR/DET do not enter the swap.

open_issues: MISMATCH (post-deadline, pre-draft trade): BOS native, slot 16. Rule at deadline is 'own' (BOS), but BOS traded the pick to OKC on 2021-06-18 (Kemba Walker/Al Horford trade), so the pre-draft holder was OKC. OKC then traded it to HOU on draft night (Sengun).

Houston/OKC/Miami/Brooklyn chain (and POR/DET eligibility for the HOU-BKN swap) is a sequential two-step swap that the pool rank grammar cannot express exactly; natives BKN/HOU/MIA/OKC share one pool object with an approximate rank allocation and the exact procedure in conditions (confidence low). Realized: HOU landed #2 (inside its top-4 protection), so HOU kept #2, OKC kept #6 and received MIA's #18; HOU held #2 and POR's #23, both better than BKN's #27, so no BKN swap - consistent with the conditions procedure, but NOT with the naive rank allocation (which would give OKC slot 2).

LAL->NOP: HR_jan21 and HR_apr21 give '8-30 protected' (NOP gets it only at 1-7, else LAL 2022 unprotected), while HR_feb21 calls the pick unprotected and the June 2019 initial report (LBS_ad19) said top-8 protected. The 8-30 version is recorded because it is the post-deadline source and matches the realized outcome (LAL kept #22; NOP got LAL's 2022 first). Whether this reflects an exercised deferral option was not confirmed.
NYK/LAC swap: the 'top-four protection' is from a single source (HR_morris20) and it is unclear which pick it protects; irrelevant at realized slots (NYK 19 better than LAC 25, no swap).
MIL->HOU is formally a swap of MIL's first for HOU's second-rounder (top-9 protected); encoded as a protected first-round rule.

Draft-night / post-draft trades ignored (pre-draft holders recorded): 10 NOP->MEM and 17 MEM->NOP (Valanciunas trade, completed after the draft), 16 OKC->HOU, 19 NYK->CHA, 21 NYK->LAC, 22 LAL->WAS->IND (Westbrook trade, completed after the draft), 25 LAC->NYK, 29 PHX->BKN, 30 UTA->MEM.
Realized-holder check: all 30 slots consistent with the rules (using the exact sequential procedure for the pool), except BOS/slot 16 (post-deadline trade, above).

LAL->NOP condition conflict (additional sources). SLAM (2019), Larry Brown Sports (2019) and Silver Screen and Roll (2024) describe it as 'top 8' and read it as NOP at 1-8; Hoops Rumors (Jan and Apr 2021, post-deadline) says '8-30 protected' (NOP only at 1-7). Kept 1-7: it is the post-deadline source and it matches the realized outcome (LAL kept #22, NOP received the 2022 pick). The two readings differ only at slot 8, which the Lakers (top-4 West at the deadline) could not reach.
